title: Different delay caps can force more upstream buffer
problem: For a fixed order on one berth, find the minimum total idle gaps that guarantee each vessel's own worst-case departure-delay cap.
failure: In the bounded example A=[0,0,0], B=[5,2,0], a common cap [5,5,5] needs total buffer 2 at [0,2,0], while caps [5,4,3] need total 4 at [0,3,1]. Using one shared cap misses stricter downstream requirements.
correction: Use each endpoint's cap H_i in every interval demand A_j+sum(B_j..B_i)-H_i, reject immediately when A_i+B_i>H_i, then compute least feasible prefixes by longest paths. The theorem is for fixed order and unit buffer cost.
transfer: When service limits differ by item, propagate each item's own bound through upstream delay chains. Do not substitute one shared cap unless that is the actual requirement.
limits: One berth, fixed order, rectangular bounded arrival/overrun uncertainty and unit buffer cost. Certificate covers n=2,3 and small integer bounds/caps only; no operational data, novelty claim or human review.
